strengths: Addresses a relevant evaluation problem: linear probing substantially underestimates information distributed across MIM patch tokens. EP is simple and offers useful control over probe capacity through query count and output dimensionality.

The empirical coverage is broad, spanning multiple backbone sizes, pretraining paradigms, and classification datasets. Reported ImageNet improvements over linear probing are substantial for MAE (+7.9 points) and SimMIM (+13.6 points).

The accuracy–parameter comparisons show promising trade-offs against numerous attentive pooling methods. Ablations examine key/value projections, attention dimensionality, and query count, with additional low-shot and intermediate-layer results.
weaknesses: The headline 10× speed-up is not demonstrated by runtime measurements. Section 4.3 compares 0.12 GFLOPs for EP with 1.44 GFLOPs for a full ViT block, while Figure 4 shows much smaller differences against closer cross-attention baselines. No training throughput, inference latency, peak memory, or end-to-end costs including the backbone are reported, leaving the central efficiency claims overstated.

The methodological novelty is limited and its implications are insufficiently analyzed. Equation (10) exactly reparameterizes learned-query attention through u_j = W_Kj^T q_j; this absorption works independently for every head. The WK-removal ablation instead restricts each query to a channel partition, changing the function class. A folded or reassociated MHCA baseline is needed to distinguish architectural benefits from parameterization and implementation choices.

Baseline fidelity raises concerns for a paper centered on systematic benchmarking. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention over all tokens, whereas their relevant aggregation mechanisms can compute only the global/class-token query. Computing unnecessary token outputs inflates their cost. The implementations and FLOP accounting require validation against the original mechanisms.

The principal comparisons are insufficiently controlled for optimization and uncertainty. Appendix C.4 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 for all probes, despite substantial architectural differences, while EP receives extensive query-count and dimensionality exploration. No repeated-run variation or confidence intervals establish whether its relatively small gains over strong attentive baselines are reliable. Hyperparameter selection splits and several training details are also unspecified.

Several conclusions exceed the evidence. EP offers strong parameter efficiency but does not uniformly outperform prior probes in accuracy: Figure 3 includes stronger competitors on SimMIM, Food-101, and Cars. Low-shot and layer-wise experiments compare primarily against linear probing, so they do not establish an advantage over existing attentive probes.

The localization analysis supports association rather than the claimed avoidance of shortcuts or improved robustness. Bounding-box attention mass lacks an area-adjusted baseline, and replacing attention with a uniform distribution mechanically perturbs low-entropy maps more strongly. No background intervention, distribution-shift evaluation, or quantitative query-diversity analysis substantiates the stronger interpretability claims.

strengths: Addresses a relevant evaluation problem: linear probing can substantially underestimate the information available in frozen MIM patch representations.

EP is simple and mathematically well motivated. Absorbing fixed learned query/key projections into full-dimensional queries reduces trainable parameters without sacrificing the corresponding attention function.

The experimental coverage is substantial, spanning multiple pretraining paradigms, backbone sizes, and classification datasets. Reported ImageNet improvements over linear probing include 67.7% to 75.6% for MAE and 51.5% to 65.1% for SimMIM.

The query-count and output-dimension ablations, low-data experiments, and intermediate-layer results provide useful practical evidence. The attention intervention analysis goes beyond qualitative visualizations alone.
weaknesses: The central efficiency claim is overstated. Figure 4 reports probe-only FLOPs, not measured speed, training time, or memory. The advertised greater-than-10× reduction compares EP against a full ViT block rather than an otherwise matched cross-attention probe. No end-to-end measurements establish the practical gain when frozen-backbone computation is included.

The contribution is principally a reparameterization, and the evaluation does not sufficiently distinguish its training benefits from avoidable implementation overhead. Equation (7) permits each head's fixed key projection and learned query to be collapsed into u_j = W_Kj^T q_j after training. Thus, conventional learned-query MHCA can use EP's attention computation at inference. Section 4.6's claim that absorption does not hold for multiple heads conflates this exact transformation with fixing W_K to identity while restricting queries to channel subspaces.

Some baseline definitions undermine the accuracy–efficiency comparison. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention over all tokens, whereas their relevant pooling/class-attention operations only require the pooled/class token as query. Computing all query outputs adds unnecessary cost. Faithful implementations and explicitly optimized baselines are necessary for a paper whose main contribution is efficiency.

Experimental tuning and uncertainty are insufficiently controlled. Appendix C.4 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 across structurally different probes, while EP receives extensive architecture sweeps. The manuscript does not establish comparable tuning budgets or explain an independent model-selection split. Results lack repeated-run uncertainty, making small gains over strong attentive baselines difficult to assess.

The localization evidence does not support claims of avoiding shortcuts, improving robustness, or ensuring complementary object-part specialization. Replacing concentrated attention with uniform attention creates a larger perturbation than replacing already diffuse attention, confounding the entropy–accuracy relationship. Bounding-box attention mass and selected visualizations do not rule out background reliance; controlled background interventions, quantitative query-diversity measures, and robustness evaluations are missing.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite useful optimizer and hardware details: exact checkpoint identifiers, weight decay, learning-rate decay, query initialization, attention scaling, and complete numerical benchmark results are not provided. Together with the baseline and efficiency issues, this prevents the otherwise promising empirical study from meeting the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Addresses a relevant evaluation problem: linear probing substantially understates the utility of frozen MIM patch representations.
EP is simple and economical. Learning full-dimensional queries directly removes redundant query/key parameterization while retaining multiple attention predictors.

The experimental coverage is broad, including multiple datasets, backbone sizes, and pretraining paradigms. Reported ImageNet gains over linear probing are substantial for MAE (67.7% to 75.6%) and SimMIM (51.5% to 65.1%).
Ablations examine query count, projection matrices, and output dimensionality; supplementary low-shot and intermediate-layer experiments provide additional evidence of practical utility.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited: Equation (10) reparameterizes the fixed learned-query attention in Equation (7) through u_j = W_Kj^T q_j. This is a useful simplification, but does not establish a more expressive attention mechanism. Consequently, the contribution depends heavily on the rigor of the benchmark and efficiency evaluation.

The advertised 10× speed-up is not demonstrated with runtime measurements. Section 4.3 compares 0.12 GFLOPs against 1.44 GFLOPs for a full ViT block, which is not a clean comparison against ordinary multi-head cross-attention. Figure 4 shows a substantially smaller computational gap to AIM. No measured training time, inference throughput, or peak memory supports the broader efficiency claims, and backbone computation is excluded.

Baseline fidelity is insufficiently established. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as self-attention over all tokens, although their pooling/class-attention operations can update only the pooled/class query. Computing unnecessary token outputs can inflate baseline costs. Reference-implementation checks and optimized cross-attention comparisons are needed.

The accuracy–parameter comparisons give EP extensive query-count and output-width sweeps, while most competitors appear at a single configuration. Figure 7 partially addresses this for AIM, but does not establish comparable budget tuning across the benchmark. A fixed learning rate on ImageNet and Places365 also leaves optimization fairness unresolved.

Reproducibility and statistical support are incomplete. The paper does not report repeated runs or uncertainty, despite several improvements over strong attentive baselines being small. Hyperparameter-selection splits, exact checkpoint identifiers, and important implementation settings are insufficiently specified. Claims of outperforming prior attentive methods across benchmarks also exceed the figures, where some competitors achieve higher accuracy.

The localization analysis supports an association, not the stronger claims about avoiding shortcuts or improving robustness. Replacing attention with a uniform distribution inherently perturbs concentrated distributions more strongly, confounding the entropy–importance relationship. Bounding-box attention and selected visualizations do not establish causal object reliance, query complementarity, or robustness under background shifts.

strengths: Addresses a relevant evaluation problem: linear probing can substantially underestimate frozen representations whose useful information is distributed across patch tokens.

EP is simple and technically well motivated. Absorbing fixed learnable queries and key projections into full-dimensional query vectors reduces trainable parameters while preserving the attention scoring function.

The empirical coverage is substantial: seven classification datasets, diverse pre-training paradigms, multiple backbone sizes, and numerous pooling baselines. Results show convincing improvements over linear probing and promising accuracy–parameter trade-offs.
The appendix provides useful experiments on query count, output dimensionality, reduced-dimensional AIM baselines, intermediate layers, limited supervision, and attention complementarity.
weaknesses: The architectural novelty is modest: EP is principally an algebraic reparameterization of learned-query cross-attention. For fixed learned queries, each head's effective vector can already be written as WK_j^T q_j. Section 4.3's suggestion that absorption does not hold for multiple heads conflates absorption with restricting queries to disjoint channel subsets. The contribution should be positioned more precisely as parameterization and optimization efficiency.

The central efficiency comparison omits important optimized baselines. Existing learned-query attention can contract key projections with queries before processing tokens, and value projection can be moved after weighted pooling using Equation 2. Comparing these implementations would distinguish intrinsic computational savings from implementation choices. Appendix B also describes CLIP and CaiT pooling as full self-attention, although their pooled/class-token outputs can be computed with only the relevant query, potentially inflating baseline costs.

Baseline tuning is insufficiently controlled for a definitive benchmark. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 and mostly uses LARS across substantially different probe architectures. EP receives extensive architectural sweeps, while comparable exploration is limited mainly to AIM. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, leaving small improvements over attentive competitors difficult to assess.

The claimed substantial compute and memory gains are not demonstrated through measured training time, throughput, or peak memory. Figure 3 reports only probe FLOPs, excluding the 17.58-GFLOP backbone that remains active throughout training. These results establish reduced probe overhead but do not establish similarly substantial savings for the complete evaluation protocol.

The abstract overstates accuracy dominance across seven benchmarks. The appendix reports cases where EP trades some accuracy for fewer parameters, including Places365 and CUB-200. The strongest supported conclusion is a favorable accuracy–parameter trade-off, rather than uniform superiority over prior attentive probing.

The interpretability and robustness claims exceed the analysis. Bounding-box attention mass, entropy, and uniform-attention interventions provide useful diagnostic correlations, but do not establish avoidance of background shortcuts or robustness. Attention diversity also does not by itself demonstrate consistent semantic part discovery; quantitative part correspondence or controlled background interventions would strengthen these claims.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant evaluation problem: global-token linear probing can underestimate representations learned through patch-level objectives. Its unified treatment of attentive pooling is useful.

The empirical coverage is substantial, spanning seven classification datasets, multiple backbone sizes, and diverse pre-training paradigms. EP delivers meaningful improvements over linear probing, including 67.7% to 75.6% for MAE ViT-B on ImageNet.
EP is simple and parameter-efficient. The appendix provides useful investigations of query count, output dimensionality, matched AIM variants, intermediate layers, and limited-data training.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited. Equation (10) directly reparameterizes each fixed learned-query attention score through u_j = W_Kj^T q_j; this absorption works independently for every head. The Section 4.3 statement that absorption does not hold for multi-head attention conflates eliminating the projection with restricting queries to channel partitions. The reported ablation tests that restriction, rather than establishing a fundamental limitation of multi-head attention.

The central benchmark does not convincingly establish superiority under appropriate optimization. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 and mostly uses LARS across substantially different probe architectures. A common training recipe need not be equally suitable for all methods. EP receives extensive architecture sweeps, while comparable baseline sweeps are largely confined to AIM on one setting. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, although several gains over attentive baselines are small.

Computational comparisons need stronger implementation controls. A fixed learned query and its key projection can be collapsed for inference, and Equation (2) permits value projection after pooling. These equivalent implementations should be considered when claiming computational savings. Appendix B also describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class-attention as full self-attention; their standard pooling/class-attention operations require only the global-token query. Computing unused patch-query outputs would inflate baseline FLOPs without improving the returned descriptor.

Practical efficiency claims exceed the measurements. Figure 3 reports only probe FLOPs, excluding the 17.58-GFLOP backbone that is recomputed during training. This is transparent but does not establish substantial end-to-end savings. No measured training time, throughput, or peak-memory comparison supports the claimed compute and memory advantages; cached-feature evaluation is explicitly left for future work.

The interpretability and robustness conclusions are stronger than the evidence. Attention mass within bounding boxes and cosine diversity do not establish semantic part correspondence or absence of background shortcuts, especially because contextualized patch features can contain information from elsewhere. Replacing sharp attention with a uniform distribution also creates a larger perturbation than replacing diffuse attention, confounding the entropy-versus-accuracy-drop analysis. Background interventions, robustness evaluations, and quantitative part annotations are absent.

The abstract's claim of outperforming prior attentive approaches across seven benchmarks overstates the results. For example, Places365 reports EP at 53.7%, below ViT at 54.84% and SigLIP at 54.39%; other results similarly demonstrate competitive accuracy with fewer parameters rather than uniformly superior accuracy. Overall, the broad experiments support a useful engineering simplification, but unresolved comparison and efficiency issues prevent the evidence from meeting the acceptance threshold.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant evaluation problem: global-token linear probing can underestimate representations learned through patch-level objectives. The unified treatment of attentive pooling methods is useful.

EP is simple and parameter-efficient, with substantial demonstrated improvements over linear probing: MAE ViT-B improves from 67.7% to 75.6%, SimMIM from 51.5% to 65.1%, and DiT from 32.7% to 57.0% on ImageNet-1K.

The experimental coverage is broad, spanning seven classification datasets, multiple backbone sizes, and diverse pre-training paradigms. The accuracy–parameter curves provide concrete evidence of useful trade-offs.

Ablations examine query count, output dimensionality, and projection matrices. Low-data and intermediate-layer experiments extend the practical findings, while attention visualizations suggest interesting specialization.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is limited: Equation (10) directly reparameterizes Equation (7) through u_j = W_Kj^T q_j. This absorption works independently for every head, preserving the attention function class. The Section 4.3 ablation instead removes W_K while restricting queries to channel subsets, so its accuracy drop does not establish that multi-head attention fundamentally requires the projection.

The computational comparison misses an important optimized baseline. Existing learned-query attention can compute W_Kj^T q_j before multiplying by X, including during training, avoiding per-token key projections without changing its parameterization. Equation (2) likewise permits value projection after pooling. Comparing these algebraically equivalent implementations is necessary to substantiate the computational advantage beyond reduced trainable parameters.

Baseline fidelity and tuning leave uncertainty around the smaller improvements over attentive competitors. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention over all tokens, whereas their pooling/class-attention operations can update only the global query. This can inflate comparator FLOPs. Appendix C.1 also fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365, while EP receives extensive architectural sweeps; equal training schedules alone do not establish equally competitive baselines.

Practical efficiency is insufficiently measured. The paper reports parameter counts and probe-only FLOPs, but no training throughput, wall-clock time, or peak memory despite claiming substantial compute and memory gains. The frozen backbone contributes 17.58 GFLOPs for MAE ViT-B and is repeatedly evaluated, so large relative savings in the probe need not translate into large end-to-end savings.

Several claims exceed the evidence. EP does not achieve the highest accuracy on every dataset; for example, Places365 results favor ViT and SigLIP. Localization correlations and complementary attention maps do not establish robustness or absence of background shortcuts. These claims require narrower wording or controlled interventions.

Results lack repeated-run uncertainty, which matters for gains of a few tenths of a percentage point over strong competitors. Reproducibility is also limited by unspecified initialization, weight decay, optimizer exceptions, and model-selection details. Overall, the empirical breadth and practical simplicity are promising, but the efficiency comparisons and baseline controls leave the paper slightly below the acceptance threshold.

strengths: Addresses an important evaluation problem: linear probing can substantially underestimate representations whose useful information is distributed across patch tokens.

EP has a clear, mathematically justified design. Absorbing fixed-query key projections into learnable full-dimensional queries preserves the attention function while reducing trainable parameters. The matched 12-predictor comparison achieves 75.1% accuracy with 1.36M parameters versus AIM's 1.95M.

The empirical scope is substantial, covering seven classification datasets, diverse pre-training paradigms, multiple backbone sizes, and numerous pooling baselines. The evidence convincingly establishes improvements over linear probing, particularly for masked-image and generative models.

The appendices provide useful additional evidence, including dimension/head ablations, limited-data experiments, retrieval transfer, and localization. LoRA+EP also demonstrates practical complementarity, reaching 76.99% on MAE ViT-B with approximately 850K trainable parameters.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is modest: EP is explicitly an equivalent reparameterization of existing learned-query attention. Its contribution therefore depends heavily on establishing a rigorous benchmark and practical efficiency advantage, rather than additional expressive capability.

Baseline computation needs closer scrutiny. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention, although their retained global-token outputs can be computed using only global-token queries. Likewise, fixed-query key projections can be reassociated as X^T(W_K^T q), avoiding per-patch key projection without changing the function. Comparisons against these optimized implementations are needed to substantiate the reported FLOP advantage.

Optimization and model-selection controls are insufficient for close accuracy comparisons. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365, despite heterogeneous architectures and parameterizations. EP receives extensive configuration sweeps; although Figure 15 partially addresses this for AIM, comparable tuning is not established across competitors. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported for improvements that are sometimes only a few tenths of a percentage point.

Practical efficiency claims exceed the measurements. The paper reports parameters and additional probe FLOPs, but not measured training time, throughput, or peak memory. The backbone costs 17.58 GFLOPs and is recomputed throughout training, so large relative savings within the probe need not yield substantial end-to-end savings. The claimed memory gains remain unquantified.

The interpretability evidence is suggestive rather than conclusive. Replacing a sharp attention distribution with uniform attention makes a larger intervention than replacing an already diffuse distribution, confounding the entropy–accuracy relationship. Bounding-box attention mass and cosine diversity do not establish semantic part specialization or avoidance of background shortcuts; controlled background interventions and quantitative part correspondence would strengthen these claims.

Several claims require correction. Table 6 calls localization 'unsupervised' despite EP being trained with image labels. Table 8 shows BEiTv2 retrieval deteriorating on Cars196, contrary to claims of consistent improvement. The limitations section also says interaction with PEFT and retrieval remain unexplored despite experiments elsewhere in the manuscript. These inconsistencies weaken the precision of the presentation.

strengths: EP is a simple, technically well-motivated reparameterization: absorbing fixed learned queries and key projections removes redundant trainable parameters without reducing the corresponding attention function class.

The evaluation is broad, covering seven classification datasets, diverse pretraining paradigms, multiple backbone sizes, and numerous pooling baselines. Improvements over linear probing are substantial for patch-oriented representations, including MAE, SimMIM, and DiT.

The matched-head AIM versus EP ablation provides concrete evidence of parameter savings at equal accuracy: 75.1% with 1.36M versus 1.95M parameters. Additional experiments on low-data learning, retrieval, and LoRA combinations strengthen the practical contribution.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is modest: the central operation follows directly from associativity of linear projections and is explicitly equivalent to existing learned-query attention. Consequently, acceptance depends heavily on the benchmark establishing reliable practical advantages, which the current comparisons do not fully resolve.

Baseline optimization is insufficiently controlled. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate to 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 and mostly uses LARS across heterogeneous architectures. EP receives extensive query-count and output-dimension sweeps, whereas equivalent baseline sweeps are limited, although Figure 15 shows that reducing AIM's output dimension also helps. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported for small differences between attentive methods.

Baseline fidelity needs clarification. Appendix B describes CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention over all tokens, whereas their standard pooling/class-attention implementations need only global/class-token queries. This discrepancy could inflate baseline FLOPs and weaken an efficiency-focused comparison.

Efficiency evidence primarily concerns trainable parameter counts and probe-only FLOPs. The paper does not substantiate its broader memory and compute claims with measured peak memory, throughput, or end-to-end training time; the shared 17.58-GFLOP backbone dominates the reported probe overhead. Moreover, the same algebra permits collapsing a trained fixed-query AIM key projection for inference, so deployment comparisons should include that equivalent implementation.

Attention analyses support associations rather than the stronger claims about robustness, avoidance of shortcuts, or semantic part discovery. Replacing attention with a uniform distribution perturbs sharper maps more strongly, complicating the interpretation of entropy versus accuracy-drop correlations. Background interventions and quantitative part-correspondence evaluation are absent. Table 6 also labels localization 'unsupervised' despite EP receiving image-level class supervision.

Several claims exceed or contradict the reported evidence. EP does not universally outperform competing attentive probes; Table 8 shows a retrieval regression for BEiTv2; and the assertion that EP at 10 epochs matches linear probing across 12 models conflicts with MAE's 60.0% versus 67.7% in Table 9. Appendix D claims an exclusively frozen-backbone evaluation despite the LoRA experiments. These inconsistencies reduce confidence in the synthesis of an otherwise substantial empirical study.

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant evaluation problem: linear probing can substantially underestimate the information available in patch-level representations.
EP has a clear, mathematically justified design. Absorbing fixed learnable queries and key projections into effective queries preserves the attention function while reducing trainable parameters.

The experimental coverage is substantial, spanning seven classification datasets and diverse pre-training paradigms. Reported ImageNet gains over linear probing include +7.9 points for MAE-B and +13.6 points for SimMIM.

The accuracy–parameter trade-offs are promising. Matched-head comparisons with AIM, dimensionality ablations, low-data experiments, and LoRA combinations provide useful evidence beyond comparisons with linear probing.
Localization, retrieval, and attention-diversity analyses offer additional evidence that the learned aggregation captures useful spatial information.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is modest: EP is principally a reparameterization of existing learnable-query attention. Its strongest contribution is therefore the empirical benchmark, making baseline fidelity and optimization particularly important.

Baseline descriptions raise concerns about efficiency comparisons. Appendix B treats CLIP pooling and CaiT class attention as full self-attention over all tokens, whereas their standard pooling/class-attention operations only require updating the global query. Computing unused patch outputs can inflate baseline FLOPs; faithful implementations and revised comparisons are needed.

The computational advantage is not fully isolated. Existing learnable-query attention can also compute W_K^T q before interacting with patches, avoiding a per-patch key projection without adopting EP's training parameterization. This algebraically optimized baseline is missing. Moreover, the paper reports probe FLOPs rather than measured training time, throughput, or peak memory, although every training iteration still executes the much larger backbone.

Optimization fairness and uncertainty are insufficiently established. Appendix C.1 fixes the learning rate at 0.1 on ImageNet and Places365 rather than tuning it per method, and does not adequately specify method-specific optimizer choices or model-selection splits. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported, which matters for the small improvements over strong attentive baselines.

Several claims exceed the evidence. Foreground attention does not establish avoidance of background shortcuts or robustness, and localization using a probe trained with ImageNet class labels is weakly supervised rather than unsupervised. The abstract's consistent superiority over prior attentive methods also overstates results where heavier probes achieve higher accuracy.

Reporting inconsistencies reduce confidence: the claim that EP at 10 epochs matches or surpasses 90-epoch linear probing across all 12 models contradicts Table 9, especially MAE-B at 60.0% versus 67.7%. The limitations section also describes PEFT interaction and retrieval as future work despite experiments already presented.
